The test image shows a corn leaf with yellowish/pale streaks running parallel to the veins, plus some scattered small tan/white spots. Key features:
- Narrow pale/yellow streaks along veins (striping pattern)
- Some small discrete tan/white lesions
- No raised pustules, no large necrotic lesions

Top candidates: **Maize_streak_virus**, **Stewarts_wilt**, **Maize_dwarf_mosaic_virus**. Let me view reference images for these.

The Maize_streak_virus reference (bottom-right panel) shows fine narrow white/yellow streaks parallel to veins — very similar to the test image. Stewarts_wilt shows seedlings with bleached streaks (different). MDMV shows broader pale banding. Let me check Physoderma_brown_spot since the test image also has scattered small spots.

Comparing all four reference images to the test image:

**Maize_streak_virus** (bottom-right panel): Narrow, fine white/yellow streaks running parallel to veins — this matches the test image's narrow longitudinal pale streaks very closely.

**Physoderma_brown_spot**: Shows small yellowish dots arranged in broad transverse bands across the leaf, with dark purple/black spots on the midrib — the test image doesn't show this transverse banding or midrib darkening.

**Maize_dwarf_mosaic_virus**: Broad, diffuse pale/white banding, not the fine narrow streaks seen in the test image.

**Stewarts_wilt**: Seedling-stage bleached streaks with vascular discoloration — doesn't match the mature leaf pattern.

The test image shows narrow, pale yellow/white streaks running longitudinally parallel to the veins on a green leaf — the hallmark of **Maize_streak_virus**. The scattered small tan spots could be secondary/early lesions consistent with early virus infection.
